variants.headline: A new government takes shape
variants.sub: The colony has a new government comprising {members}.
variants.body:
A new government comprising {members} has been formed. Its formation establishes an administration; it does not establish the success of its future decisions. In considering {target}, the useful distinction is between assembling a government and meeting the obligations that come with governing.

There is a new government. Now comes the difficult part of being one. A ministry can look splendid as an idea; people still have to live under its decisions. Keep the ceremonial satisfaction in proportion, and save some attention for what public office is supposed to accomplish.

We are unconvinced by {target}. The completion of an arrangement for office does not deserve to be mistaken for political merit; the public is entitled to a more demanding standard. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.

variants.headline: Formation is the beginning of governing
variants.sub: Government formation has produced an administration comprising {members}.
variants.body:
The colony has a new government comprising {members}. The new administration in {colony} gives public attention an institutional focus, while leaving its practical record to be made. variants.headline: New ministry, practical obligations
variants.sub: A new government comprising {members} has been formed.
variants.body:
Government formation has produced an administration comprising {members}. There is an obvious temptation to read a whole political future into that fact. A more useful approach to {target} begins with the administration that has actually been formed and the responsibilities inherent in exercising public authority.
